gen-dafont-early-gameboy-inter: Inter reads smooth and tube-like, its big counters opening up a tall lowercase. Early GameBoy is the showoff here, stretched out and playful, while Inter just keeps the text easy to follow.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-mulish: Chunky and cheeky, with room to spare. Mulish keeps its line weight ruler-straight and its large lowercase open, so paragraphs under Early GameBoy's modest thick-thin swagger move along smoothly.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-roboto-slab: Playful swagger meets sturdy structure. Early GameBoy stretches out with a skyward x-height, and Roboto Slab, a slab-serif with open throats, gives the pairing its best quality: a firm middle zone that anchors every line.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-rubik: Rubik's lowercase looks big next to its capitals, and its round shapes stay clear even small. Early GameBoy does the loud, widely spaced showing off, and Rubik does the soft, steady talking.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-bitter: Grounded and dependable, Bitter brings a slab-serif frame with a huge lowercase eye. And Edo SZ, built on one constant stroke width, would carry that over a longer passage with a sturdy, cast-iron feel.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-epunda-slab: Edo SZ stands tall in cast-iron lowercase, drawn with a single stroke width from start to finish. Epunda Slab, with its gaping c, probably wants a generous size.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-glegoo: Cast-iron stature, one fixed stroke, no fuss. And Edo SZ handles the bold, skeletal display work, while Glegoo, a text serif with wide unclosed mouths, handles the refined, editorial reading.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-hanuman: Edo SZ stands out for its pipe-cleaner letterforms, a lowercase as tall as cast-iron capitals. Hanuman, a text serif with a high-waisted lowercase, adds traditional refinement, and that gap in texture is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-kadwa: Kadwa reads large and open, its serif curves never quite closing. Against Edo SZ's thick-only outline, the pair's strongest quality is a classic editorial voice with real presence.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-piazzolla: Edo SZ's cast-iron lowercase never pinches or swells, keeping one constant stroke throughout. Piazzolla, a classic serif with lowercase nearly matching its capitals, follows with an authoritative, refined text that sits easily beneath it.
